title: Pott disease as named spinal TB
dek: Percivall Pott's eponym for tuberculous spondylitis. An anatomy-and-history card that must hand off to EPTB diagnosis, not to a unique backbone invented on Wikipedia.
story: Pott disease is Wikipedia's eponym for tuberculous infection of the spine — vertebral osteomyelitis, often with a cold abscess and kyphosis in neglected disease. The organism is MTBC. The name is 18th-century surgery, not a separate species.

Modern care is imaging plus microbiology plus WHO TB treatment, with orthopedic decisions that this glossary will not script. Steroids are not automatically 'the Pott protocol' copied from meningitis.
Differential includes pyogenic osteomyelitis, malignancy, and brucellosis in the right geography. The eponym does not close those.
deep: A Gibbus deformity is a late anatomic headline, not an early sensitive sign.
NAAT on pus/tissue is the WRD logic from the EPTB diagnosis plate.
Paraplegia risk is why this site is high-stakes; that still does not make Wikipedia a neurosurgical manual.
Pediatric spinal TB exists; dosing stays on pediatric treatment plates.

visual.caption: Schematic spine-as-site: vertebra, disc, cold abscess. The eponym names the pattern; it does not replace a specimen from one of these layers.

example.title: Kyphosis without microbiology
example.setup: Radiology: 'consistent with Pott'. No NAAT. Team wants HRZE from the eponym alone.

steps.title: Eponym is a differential, not a culture
Look for pulmonary/miliary pairing
steps.body: Spine is allowed to be the tip of disseminated disease.

steps.title: Then treat as TB disease with DST class
steps.body: The name does not pick Group A drugs.

example.takeaway: Pott is a site eponym. Microbiology still has to speak.
